label: E12
headline: First Convoys Transit Strait of Meridia Since Blockade Began
body: QOROS — The first organized convoys passed through the Strait of Meridia in both directions on Sunday, marking the initial movement of commercial vessels since the Republic of Varessa imposed a naval blockade in May 2026. HarborTrack data confirms that daily transit counts reached approximately 53 ships, roughly 38 percent of the pre-crisis baseline of 140 commercial transits per day. The movement follows the announcement of Operation Open Water on 20 August, a five-nation escort framework involving Khoreth, Sundaria, Elbar, Aldenport, and Virelles. Varessan Coastal Forces maintained a visible presence at the channel’s edges but did not intercept the escorted groups. Representatives of the Meridian Compact stated that the passage demonstrates the operational viability of the coalition’s security guarantees. The Varessan government in Ostrev declined to comment on the specific transits, reiterating its position that the blockade remains in effect until diplomatic conditions are met. Qoros mediators have scheduled a follow-up session to review the safety protocols established for the escort corridors. Insurance underwriters in Qoros reported immediate adjustments to risk assessments as the first shipments cleared the chokepoint.
